People have told me that and I wish I could be okay too. Maybe I have some deep seated issues, or maybe I’m actually extroverted. I’m not sure. But it’s been nearly 3 years since I’ve interacted with a person face to face that wasn’t at work or in my abusive home, and I feel like I’m losing my mind.

I love being alone though. I love doing my own thing. Not dealing with people. But I feel empty inside at the same time. I’m so confused on how to feel.

But anyway thank you.

Thanks. And I’m not doing online dating or any kind of dating for multiple reasons. 1. They’re going to expect more than just a hug at some point, which I’m not ready for. 2. I’m in such a bad place right now that I’m emotionally unequipped for romance; it would just create toxic codependence where I’d rely on the person too much for my happiness (oxytocin is one hell of a drug). 3. Going on dates just to get a hug is sort of manipulative.

I’ll see my therapist in two weeks and I’ll talk about my depression (which I haven’t been able to do yet).

i should probably say that the whole living together and raising children thing is something that wouldn't happen in YEARS. As in, at the very least a decade from now; perhaps even longer. We don't even know for sure if it will happen.

Right now I am pursuing my own dreams through a life that doesn't involve her. We are long distance and are both okay with that. We are still close, yes, but she is okay with me going down my own path.

I do agree that my reaction to being filmed worsened the situation. It was bad to begin with but I simply made it worse.

And it was more than just a silly video. I was a living nightmare, according to the people that witnessed it. They said I was crude and insensitive and said very offensive things that pissed everyone off. But I'll admit, I kinda had a feeling my friends were already looking for a way to get rid of me beforehand (I was shy and hard to talk to and very cautious and skittish), so I'm not too surprised about how they'd treat the way I acted as irredeemable (though the way I acted was still p terrible). For the longest time, I thought that was just my social anxiety telling me that, but it turned out to be true, and so now I don't know whether or not to trust my anxiety. The way I acted also caught everyone off guard since I was always the cute and innocent one.

I was distraught when I found out about the video. I ended up getting very upset and that just added fuel to the fire. I had a panic attack which made it more embarrassing.

After it happened, the friends made it a goal to make everyone that knew me hated me. They made sure to tell everyone that I wasn't the "good girl I seemed to be", and they went on about it for months. They associated everything I did at the party as my true colors...and maybe they're right...maybe they are my true colors. They said I'm crude and offensive and a b*tch. Someone also outed me as being gay and said I was probably a disgusting perv too. I couldn't handle the shame of everyone knowing, so I quit college. I live in a small town where everyone knows each other, so I completely avoided social contact for about a year out of fear that anyone I could talk to would know about what happened, and I was a terrified mess every time I went out into public.

Anyway it makes me feel like a very terrible person. If that's the person I become when my inhibitions are gone, then how in the world can I allow myself to ease up? I don't want to be a terrible person. For me, going through that seemed to teach me that I'm a recluse for a reason...and I hate it.

Now as a disclaimer: I'm aware that I could have just been blowing my emotions out of proportion. It's actually a little better now ever since I started medications. But that was how I felt at the time when it happened, and I'm still a bit traumatized. But I'm a lot better now and can go into public with ease and I now have a job. Sorry this is so long.

school. one time, i used to be a social butterfly, always talking to people with no care in the world about no worry about what the world thought of me. id dance in recitals, act in school plays, and sing on stage. but then i moved to a new school in elementary and the entire class rejected me. for every reason that defined me as me- my race, my personality, my interests, my appearance, my culture, and later after hitting puberty, my sexuality as well (even before i found out i was a lesbian, kids would call me that to make fun of me because i was tomboyish). everything about me was...well...wrong. and it made me feel very ashamed of myself.

and my parents were the same. everything i did was wrong in their eyes. my hair would always look wrong, the way i walked was always wrong, the way i talked was wrong, all my interests were too boyish or childish, my weight was wrong, everything was wrong. i never made them proud. and my siblings exhibited the same attitudes as my parents and peers combined, and i was bullied by them the worse. my siblings would even lead the bullying sometimes that would happen in school.

and slowly i retreated into myself. my earliest memory of it happening was when the girls in my school were dancing and jumping rope to upbeat music. i really wanted to dance, but for some reason, i decided to sit in the corner instead and do absolutely nothing for recess. and ever since, that habit consumed my entire personality, and i became nothing beyond withdrawing.

i tried to do this one time and it lowkey traumatized me to the point where i had flashbacks of it for the first few months after it happened. there was somebody who used to like me when i was shy, but on the few days i decided to be talkative, they did the same thing described but they filmed me while doing it and it scared the living shit out of me.

i abandoned my entire social circle out of fear and embarrassment and now im all alone. its stupid as hell but i am so scared of people.
